audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers gave Level 1 to Irelia while the packet chart and whys[0] both say the stage is even.
audit.why: At Level 1 Irelia has no stun, no Ionian Fervor stacks and one point in Bladesurge; Nasus only wants Siphoning Strike last-hits. Neither side can commit.
audit.corrected: Level 1 = Skill (5/10) in phases[0].side and win[0] together. Rows 1-6 already agree across layers and with the packet.

audit.why: Spike order is right: Irelia's level-3 E window, level-6 Vanguard's Edge wall, first item, then Nasus reclaiming at 2+ items with stacked Siphoning Strike and Fury of the Sands (120/100/80s).
audit.corrected: First-item spike renamed from Trinity Force to Blade of the Ruined King so it matches the itemization block on the same page.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page repeatedly credits Irelia's passive with 'armor shred' (whys[3], whys[5], spikes[2].text, mid). Ionian Fervor grants stacking bonus Attack Speed and, at max stacks, bonus damage on hit. It shreds nothing.
audit.why: Riot kit text for Irelia's passive: 'When Irelia strikes enemies with spells she gains stacking bonus Attack Speed. At maximum stacks she also gains bonus damage on hit.' The mirror audit on nasus__irelia found the identical error six times and corrected it the same way.
audit.corrected: Attack speed and bonus on-hit damage, not armour shred. This also makes Wither the direct counter — it cuts the exact stat Irelia is stacking, which is why the mid-game window closes when it lands.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing told the player that Siphoning Strike is an auto-attack reset, so they read the cast as the danger cue.
audit.why: Kit flag autoReset on Nasus Q; missingInteractions rule autoreset-burst-tell. The auto wind-up, not the ability cast, is the moment to step out.
audit.corrected: Added to dosFull[2].d: the wind-up is the tell.

audit.whatIsWrong: Itemization gave no warning that Fury of the Sands deals percent-max-health damage.
audit.why: missingInteractions rule resistances-invalidated; kit flag percentHealth on Nasus R. Stacking raw HP feeds it.

audit.whatIsWrong: dontsFull[1].d carried boilerplate about wasting your own cooldown under a title about his Wither slow.
audit.why: Wither is 15/14/13/12/11s — long enough that baiting it opens a real window.
audit.corrected: Concrete number and the bait-then-engage sequence.

edits.before: Stack passive on the wave before any trade. Identify how Nasus contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Level 1 is even — he only wants Siphoning Strike last-hits. Deny the cannon and stack Ionian Fervor off the wave.

edits.before: Max Bladesurge stacks give you bonus on-hit damage and armor shred, letting you out-DPS an immobile, pre-stacked Nasus in every short skirmish.
edits.after: Max Ionian Fervor stacks give bonus attack speed and on-hit damage, letting you out-DPS an immobile, unstacked Nasus in every short skirmish.

edits.before: Your Trinity Force / first-item spike with full reset uptime and stacked passive shred makes you a lane tyrant who dives him off CS.
edits.after: Your Blade of the Ruined King spike with full reset uptime and max Ionian Fervor attack speed makes you a lane tyrant who dives him off CS.

edits.before: Your Trinity Force / core spike plus max Bladesurge stacks (bonus on-hit + armor shred) makes you a lane tyrant who should be diving him off CS.
edits.after: Your Blade of the Ruined King spike plus max Ionian Fervor stacks (attack speed into bonus on-hit) makes you a lane tyrant who dives him off CS.

edits.before: This is your window. Bait his W (Wither) with a fake step-in, and the moment it's down E-stun into a Q-reset, build to max Bladesurge stacks and shred his armor while he's immobile. If he Withers you mid-trade, hold W (Defiant Dance) to tank his autos with the damage reduction while the slow runs out, then keep resetting off the wave. At 6 your R (Vanguard's Edge) wall traps him short of tower so he can't slow-walk out of your all-in, and your first item makes every dive lethal.
edits.after: This is your window. Bait his W (Wither) with a fake step-in — it's 15s at rank 1 — and the moment it's down E-stun into a Q-reset, stacking Ionian Fervor to max for the attack speed and bonus on-hit while he's immobile. If he Withers you mid-trade, hold W (Defiant Dance) to tank his autos with the damage reduction while the slow runs out, then keep resetting off the wave. At 6 your R (Vanguard's Edge) wall traps him short of tower so he can't slow-walk out of your all-in.

edits.before: Nasus wastes Wither — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: His Siphoning Strike is an auto reset — the wind-up is the tell.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Wither is 15s at rank 1 — bait it, then E-stun in while it's gone.

edits.before: Start Doran's Blade + pot. Core: Blade of the Ruined King  (%HP + the duel spike), then Wit's End / Sterak's Gage; boots Plated Steelcaps. Executioner's Calling early — his healing fights your pattern.
edits.after: Start Doran's Blade + pot. Core: Blade of the Ruined King (%HP + the duel spike), then Wit's End / Sterak's Gage; boots Plated Steelcaps. Fury of the Sands burns %max HP — anti-heal, not raw HP, answers his sustain.

notes: The 'armor shred' claim for Irelia's passive appeared four times in this entry and is the same wrong mental model the mirror audit (nasus__irelia) found on the other side. Ionian Fervor is stacking attack speed plus bonus on-hit at max stacks — which is exactly why Wither, an attack-speed slow, is the counter. Level 1 flipped to Skill in matched full/content pairs to agree with the packet chart and with whys[0].
